# 11. TIME SERIES ANALYSIS - Using adjusted values

```{r}

library(tidyverse)
library(networkD3)
library(plotly)
library(scales)

```

```{r}
setwd("D:/work/JHU/Final-project")
movies <- readRDS("data/movies_clean.rds")

movies <- readRDS("data/movies_clean.rds")

create_time_series_analysis <- function(data) {
  if (!"Year" %in% colnames(data)) {
    if ("Released_year" %in% colnames(data)) {
      data <- data %>% dplyr::mutate(Year = Released_year)
    } else if ("Released" %in% colnames(data)) {
      data <- data %>% dplyr::mutate(Year = lubridate::year(Released))
    } else {
      stop("No Year or Released_year column found in dataset.")
    }
  }

  yearly_stats <- data %>%
    dplyr::group_by(Year) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      total_revenue = sum(BoxOffice_adjusted, na.rm = TRUE) / 1e9,
      movie_count   = dplyr::n(),
      avg_rating    = mean(imdbRating, na.rm = TRUE),
      avg_runtime   = mean(Runtime_num, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups       = "drop"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::filter(Year >= 2000)

  ts_plot <- plotly::plot_ly(yearly_stats) %>%

    plotly::add_trace(
      x = ~Year,
      y = ~total_revenue,
      type = "scatter",
      mode = "lines+markers",
      name = "Total Revenue (2024 adj.)",
      line   = list(color = "darkblue", width = 3),
      marker = list(size = 7),
      text = ~paste0(
        "Year: ", Year,
        "<br>Total Revenue: ", round(total_revenue, 2), " B$",
        "<br>Movie Count: ", movie_count,
        "<br>Avg Rating: ", round(avg_rating, 2),
        "<br>Avg Runtime: ", round(avg_runtime, 1), " min"
      ),
      hovertemplate = "%{text}<extra></extra>"
    ) %>%

    plotly::add_trace(
      x = ~Year,
      y = ~movie_count / 100,
      type = "scatter",
      mode = "lines+markers",
      name = "Movie Count (÷100)",
      yaxis = "y2",
      line   = list(color = "darkgreen", width = 2),
      marker = list(size = 6)
    ) %>%

    plotly::add_trace(
      x = ~Year,
      y = ~avg_rating,
      type = "scatter",
      mode = "lines+markers",
      name = "Avg Rating",
      yaxis = "y3",
      line   = list(color = "firebrick", width = 2),
      marker = list(size = 6)
    ) %>%

    plotly::add_trace(
      x = ~Year,
      y = ~avg_runtime,
      type = "scatter",
      mode = "lines+markers",
      name = "Avg Runtime (min)",
      yaxis = "y4",
      line   = list(color = "orange", width = 2),
      marker = list(size = 6)
    ) %>%

    plotly::layout(
      title = "Movie Industry Trends Over Time (Inflation-Adjusted)",
      xaxis = list(title = "Year"),

      yaxis = list(
        title = "Total Revenue (Billion USD, 2024 adj.)",
        side  = "left",
        titlefont = list(color = "darkblue"),
        tickfont  = list(color = "darkblue"),
        linecolor = "darkblue",
        tickcolor = "darkblue"
      ),

      yaxis2 = list(
        title     = "Movie Count (÷100)",
        overlaying = "y",
        side       = "right",
        showgrid   = FALSE,
        titlefont = list(color = "darkgreen"),
        tickfont  = list(color = "darkgreen"),
        linecolor = "darkgreen",
        tickcolor = "darkgreen"
      ),

      yaxis3 = list(
        title      = "Average Rating",
        overlaying = "y",
        side       = "right",
        position   = 0.95,
        showgrid   = FALSE,
        range      = c(5.5, 7.0),
        titlefont = list(color = "firebrick"),
        tickfont  = list(color = "firebrick"),
        linecolor = "firebrick",
        tickcolor = "firebrick"
      ),

      yaxis4 = list(
        title      = "Average Runtime (minutes)",
        overlaying = "y",
        side       = "left",
        position   = 0.05,
        showgrid   = FALSE,
        titlefont = list(color = "orange"),
        tickfont  = list(color = "orange"),
        linecolor = "orange",
        tickcolor = "orange"
      ),

      hovermode = "x unified",
      legend    = list(orientation = "h", x = 0.2, y = -0.1),
      margin    = list(l = 80, r = 120, t = 60, b = 60)
    )

  return(ts_plot)
}





```

```{r}
ts_plot <- create_time_series_analysis(movies)
ts_plot 
```

```{r} 
htmlwidgets::saveWidget(ts_plot, "time_series_4metrics.html", selfcontained = TRUE)
```
